SUMMARY: Offline queue: drain race, delete conflicts, failed inserts, expiry, singleton
USER_STORY: As a user who edits offline, I want every queued change to either sync or tell me why it did not, so nothing vanishes and nothing retries forever.
DESCRIPTION: src/lib/offlineQueue.ts, src/hooks/useNetworkStatus.ts, src/hooks/useAccounts.ts, useCategories.ts, QueueReviewSheet.tsx, tests/offlineQueue.test.mjs. Backlog items from the LED-05 and LED-53 retros, all still open: (1) drainQueue ends with writeQueue(remaining), clobbering anything enqueued or resolved mid-drain (pre-existing race; the sheet buttons are disabled while syncing as a mitigation only). (2) An update whose server row was deleted: maybeSingle returns null, the update hits 0 rows and is counted as synced. (3) Conflict detection is update-only; delete conflicts are undetected. (4) Inserts and deletes that fail with a database error retry forever with no failure state. (5) Expiry is evaluated only on drain, so an offline item does not flag until the next sync. (6) The review sheet lacks per-item detail of what changed (mine vs theirs). (7) useNetworkStatus is not a singleton: each call attaches its own listeners and the online handler drains, so a second call races the first (LED-53 retro learned). Make it one provider. (8) updateAccountOrder and updateCategoryOrder still silently no-op offline. (9) drainQueue and keepTheirs have no tests because there is no supabase or localStorage mock harness; add one. Read knowledge/patterns/offline-queue-conflict-handling.md first. Keep 'gold for pending, red only for genuine failure' (LED-116 depends on the gold token).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A drain never overwrites an item enqueued or resolved while it ran (test); (b) an update to a row deleted on the server becomes a 'conflict' item, not 'synced' (test); (c) delete conflicts are detected and offered keep mine or keep theirs; (d) a repeated database error moves an insert or delete to a failed state after a bounded number of tries and shows it in the banner and sheet; (e) items flag as expired when the clock passes the limit, not only on the next drain; (f) the sheet shows changed fields for a conflict; (g) useNetworkStatus is provided once and a second consumer cannot start a second drain; (h) reorder while offline says so instead of silently doing nothing; (i) a mock supabase and localStorage harness covers drainQueue and keepTheirs; (j) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Partial-failure paths: account adjustment, undo, sign-out
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a write that half-succeeded to say so and offer the missing step, not to report total failure or silently leave a gap.
DESCRIPTION: src/hooks/useAccounts.ts (updateAccountWithAdjustment), src/hooks/useUndoDelete.ts, src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx LED-93 retro Backlog and LED-11 retro Backlog. (1) updateAccountWithAdjustment can half-succeed: the account saves, then the balance-adjustment transaction fails, and it returns an error as if nothing saved. Move it to the partial-failure + Fix pattern LED-93 built for card payments (NotificationContext, useNotify), where Fix reruns only the failed step. (2) Undo restores the same fields as before LED-93 and drops tags and goal_id; carry them through. (3) deleteAccount's final supabase.auth.signOut() result is ignored (LED-11 retro); surface it as an auth failure. (4) LED-11 retro: the profile-fetch banner shows even when a cached profile is on screen; suppress it when a cache exists. The split write is LED-130.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A failed adjustment after a saved account shows 'Account saved, balance adjustment not recorded' with a Fix that retries only the adjustment and never saves the account twice; (b) undo of a deleted transaction restores tags and goal_id; (c) a failed final signOut in deleteAccount is shown to the user; (d) the profile-fetch banner is suppressed while a cached profile is displayed; (e) pure parts (which steps remain, what an undo restores) are unit-tested in src/lib; (f) lint, build and test pass.

USER_STORY: As a user splitting a transaction, I want the split to succeed or fail as one action and keep my tags and receipt, so a failure never leaves the amount counted twice.
DESCRIPTION: src/pages/TransactionsPage.tsx (handleSplitConfirm), supabase/migrations (new), src/components/transactions/SplitTransactionDialog.tsx LED-81 and LED-93 retro Backlogs. handleSplitConfirm writes the lines one at a time and then deletes the original with 'await deleteTransaction(splittingTx.id)' whose result is ignored; a failure part-way leaves partial lines plus the original, and a failed delete leaves both (the amount is counted twice). It also drops tags, receipt and subcategory. The dialog now states the loss honestly (LED-81); this ticket removes it. Add a plpgsql function split_transaction(original_id uuid, lines jsonb) SECURITY INVOKER (RLS applies; never bypass it client-side per AGENTS.md) that inserts the children, carries tags, receipt_url, subcategory_id and goal_id, deletes the original and returns the new ids, all in one transaction. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A split is one rpc call that either writes every line and removes the original or changes nothing; (b) tags, receipt, subcategory and goal_id carry to every child; (c) account balances are unchanged by a split (checked on a local database); (d) failure shows the notification surface with Retry; (e) splitting offline is refused with a message; (f) the migration applies cleanly to an empty database and to seed.sql; (g) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Unitemised loan debt: add it as a purchase, atomically
USER_STORY: As a user whose loan balance is larger than its itemised purchases, I want to itemise the gap in one step, so the warning goes away instead of reappearing.
DESCRIPTION: src/components/accounts/LoanPurchaseTracker.tsx, src/components/accounts/LoanPurchaseForm.tsx, src/hooks/useLoanPurchases.ts, supabase/migrations (new) [14a] LED-82 retro Decisions and Backlog. The design's 'Add it as a purchase' was not built: adding a purchase raises the account balance by its total, so the gap would never close. It needs one atomic write that creates the purchase and lowers the loan balance by the gap; two client writes can leave the debt counted twice. Add a function add_unitemised_purchase(account_id uuid, purchase jsonb) SECURITY INVOKER that inserts the financed purchase and reduces the account balance by the gap in one transaction, and returns the purchase. The band's action opens LoanPurchaseForm pre-filled with the gap as principal. Also from the LED-82 retro: right after a purchase is created useLoanPurchases refetches before the page refetches the account, so a false gap can flash for one render; fix by awaiting both or invalidating together. Follow knowledge/rules/no-manual-memo-on-derived-values.md for the gap figure. The migration must apply cleanly to an empty database.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The reconciliation band offers 'Add it as a purchase', which opens the purchase form with the gap prefilled; (b) saving calls one rpc that creates the purchase and lowers the balance; afterwards the two figures agree and the band disappears; (c) a failed write changes nothing (checked with a forced failure); (d) no false-gap flash after creation (checked in the browser); (e) the migration applies cleanly to an empty database; (f) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Exchange-rate source, prefill and original amount
USER_STORY: As a user with money in more than one currency, I want totals to convert at a rate I trust and imports to remember the original amount, not exclude or mix.
DESCRIPTION: DECIDED 2026-09-26 - OD-3 (b): rates come from a live feed (a free API with no key, called from the browser; Frankfurter, the ECB feed, is the candidate and must be checked to cover the user's currencies before building), stored in the existing exchange_rates row (base, rates, overrides, as_of). The user chooses how often rates refresh: every time the app opens, daily, weekly or manual only (default daily), stored as a new profiles column (the one migration in this ticket). A pure src/lib function decides whether a refresh is due from that setting and as_of; a Refresh now control forces one. A failed fetch keeps the last stored rates, shows their date and says the refresh failed; a currency with no rate is never guessed. Manual overrides in exchange_rates.overrides win over fetched rates. Then, as originally scoped: supabase/migrations/20260920100100_add_exchange_rates_and_transaction_checks.sql, src/lib/importCurrency.ts, src/lib/accountsOverview.ts, src/hooks/useBudgets.ts LED-75, LED-76, LED-03 and LED-23 retro Backlogs. The exchange_rates table exists but nothing fills it or reads it on the client. (a) a rate lookup in src/lib; (b) the Import currency row prefills the rate (LED-75 'No automatic rate'); (c) a converted import stores the original amount and currency so re-importing the same foreign statement at a different rate is still caught by duplicate detection (LED-75); (d) Accounts, Home, Reports and Budgets convert unrated totals instead of excluding them, retiring most UnratedCurrencyNotice sites (LED-03, LED-76, LED-135); (e) mixed-currency totals stop rendering 'A + B' (LED-23); (f) cross-currency transfers get a second rate (LED-75). **Fallback:** totals count only the default currency and name the excluded currencies (LED-76, LED-135), Budgets exclude unrated spend with UnratedCurrencyNotice (LED-03), and an import in another currency needs a manually typed rate; nothing is converted silently.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) OD-3 is answered (b, live feed with a user-set refresh frequency) and recorded; (b) a tested lookup returns a rate or 'no rate', honouring overrides; (c) a tested pure function says whether a refresh is due for each frequency setting; (d) a failed fetch keeps the stored rates and is shown, not swallowed; (e) Settings has a refresh frequency control and a Refresh now button; (f) import prefills the rate and keeps the original amount and currency; (g) Accounts, Home, Reports and Budgets agree on converted totals; (h) the migration applies cleanly to an empty database; (i) lint, build and test pass.
